chunks: And this hadith has been narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever listens intently to a letter from the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, without himself reciting, God will write for him a good deed, erase an evil deed from him, and raise him a level. Whoever recites it looking (from the text) without a voice, God will write for him, for every letter, a good deed, erase an evil deed from him, and raise him a level. Whoever learns a letter from it openly (by heart), God will write for him ten good deeds, erase ten evil deeds from him, and raise him ten levels.
He said: I do not say for every verse, but for every letter — 'Ba', or 'Ta', or the likes of these two.

He said: And whoever recites a letter clearly while seated in his salat, God will write for him, because of it, fifty good deeds, erase fifty evil deeds from him, and raise him fifty levels. And whoever recites a letter while standing in his salat, God will write for him, for every letter, one hundred good deeds, erase one hundred evil deeds from him, and raise him one hundred levels.
And whoever completes it (the Quran), there will be for him an answered supplication — either deferred or hastened.
He (the narrator) said: I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you — completing all of it?' He said: 'Completing all of it.'

key_terms.حَرْف: Letter (of the Arabic alphabet); the basic unit of Quranic reward in this hadith — not the verse (ayah)
key_terms.حَسَنَة: Good deed/merit — a unit of divine reward recorded in one's spiritual account
key_terms.خَتَمَ: To complete/seal the recitation of the entire Quran (khatam al-Quran)
key_terms.دَرَجَة: Level or rank in paradise — elevated through Quranic recitation
key_terms.دَعْوَة مُسْتَجَابَة: Answered supplication — promised to one who completes the Quran
key_terms.سَيِّئَة: Evil deed/sin — expiated through Quranic engagement

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting and listening to the Quran according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), narrating a hadith originally attributed to Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him), outlines a graduated scale of divine rewards for different modes of engaging with the Quran: listening without reciting earns one reward per letter, silent reading earns one per letter, memorization earns ten per letter, reciting while seated in prayer earns fifty per letter, and reciting while standing in prayer earns one hundred per letter. The hadith concludes with the promise of an answered supplication for completing the entire Quran. This teaching encouraged early Muslims to engage with the Quran in all available ways, even when full recitation was not possible, and emphasized that the reward is per letter — not per verse — making every individual sound of the Quran spiritually significant.
